critical_conditions: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome Type 3 - genetic connective tissue disorder requiring gentle handling, high bleeding risk, joint instability
POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome) - requires IV fluids, lying flat, slow position changes, continuous cardiac monitoring
Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis - inflammatory condition requiring immunosuppressive management
Obstructive Sleep Apnea - may require respiratory support
medications_to_avoid: Ketorolac (Toradol) - documented severe allergy with swelling reaction
Any NSAIDs similar to ketorolac - cross-reactivity likely
allergy_alerts: Latex - SEVERE: use latex-free gloves and equipment

emergency_steps: Notify provider of EDS diagnosis and POTS condition before treatment
Access MySaintLukes and University Health portals for full medical history
Monitor heart rate and blood pressure continuously (baseline HR elevated due to POTS)
Establish IV access for potential fluid support (POTS management)
Gentle handling for all procedures due to EDS - avoid aggressive manipulation
Note: baseline vital signs may appear abnormal due to POTS - tachycardia is expected
emergency_protocol.baseline_vital_sign_notes: Patient has POTS, so elevated heart rate (111 bpm) is normal baseline. Do not be alarmed by tachycardia. Patient also has EDS with connective tissue fragility.
emergency_protocol.physical_handling_notes: EDS Type 3 patients have fragile connective tissue, easy bruising, and joint hypermobility. Use extreme care with joint manipulation and blood pressure measurements. Gentle handling required for all physical contact.
